target_customer: Medical, dental and dermatology practices and their rollups that pay for AI phone and text agents
problem: Practice front desks miss calls and spend staff time on scheduling, intake and insurance checks, which costs revenue and labor.
business_model: B2B SaaS, AI voice and text agents sold to healthcare practices
product_category: AI receptionist and practice administration for healthcare

founders.name: Oliver Silverstein
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked on streamlining chip design with cloud technology at ARM and built an AI to track student outcomes for Northeastern.

founders.name: Eric Mei
education: Cornell University, BS/M.Eng in Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Software engineer at LinkedIn on job posting quality and communications, per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time voice agents with integrations into practice management systems such as Dentrix, Eaglesoft, athenahealth and eClinicalWorks. The integrations and reliability were harder than the model layer.

defensibility.rationale: Voice agent building blocks were widely available in 2024, so copying was feasible. Integrations with practice software and workflow tuning give some lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from sources. Several funded healthcare voice AI startups were selling to the same buyers by 2025.

market_need_then: The company claims its agents cut labor cost and raise booking rates. These are company claims on the YC page. Independent demand evidence from 2024 was not collected.

branding.domain_note: Uses opencall.ai. The company is listed as OpenCall.ai in some directories.

identity.logo: Simple logo mark per site visit
identity.visual_style: Clean and modern with line icons, customer logos and dashboard screenshots
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct with punchy headlines and bold statistics

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand itself was found. The name is generic in a crowded AI voice agent field.

pivots.from: AI call centers for any business (YC launch post framing)
pivots.to: AI agents focused on healthcare practices
pivots.why: YC listing and site now center on healthcare practice administration. Date and reason not stated.

outcome_analysis: OpenCall is active with a seven person team and named healthcare customers on its site. Its early positioning was call centers for any business and it later narrowed to healthcare practices. Funding is unclear, with aggregators giving conflicting totals, so strength of traction cannot be judged from verified rounds.
notes: Funding unverified: one aggregator reports 6M pre-seed announced Feb 2024 with CoreNest Capital and YC, CB Insights lists 500K on 2024-03-10. Neither confirmed by a press release or company source so no round recorded. Competitor searches returned only 2025 and 2026 comparison pages, so the dated list is empty. Nicholas Lee appears in a team photo but is not listed as a founder on the YC page. Completeness pass: the pre-seed of 6M dated 2024-02 rests on VCBacked and a Signalbase listing, aggregators only; CB Insights lists 500K as a convertible note on 2024-03-10, which conflicts and is not summed.
